title: bug: the JetBrains plugin judges a Docker-run daemon's .moe/daemon.json by its container pid (MoeDaemonSupervisor.isReachable requires isProcessAlive(pid) unless the path has the WSL form), so on project open it deletes the live daemon's daemon.json and spawns a second daemon on the same .moe/ (JetBrains twin of task-da89f620)
description:
Filed by hunt #23 (task-da51c48b), from the same real-docker run at moe/work-2026-10-24 2037e856 as task-da89f620. Read that row's EVIDENCE first.
- The container daemon writes {"port":19877,"pid":15,...,"bindHost":"0.0.0.0"} into the mounted project's .moe/daemon.json.
- /health answers healthy for the project, and a host moe-proxy bridges to it.
- On the host, `kill -0 15` reports "No such process".

PROBLEM (code at 2037e856)
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:948-952:
  `isReachable = (isOtherSideOfWsl(info.projectPath, isWindows()) || isProcessAlive(info.pid)) && isPortOpen(info.port)`
  - isOtherSideOfWsl only recognizes the WSL/Windows path form.
  - A container record has a native path, so the dead host pid makes it unreachable.
- MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:153-176: the start path then sees no live daemon. `deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged(info)` removes the record ("Removed stale daemon.json (PID 15 not reachable or another project)"), and the supervisor spawns its own daemon.
- MoeProjectService.kt:177-188: connect() does the same ("Removed stale daemon.json in connect() (PID 15 not reachable)") and schedules a reconnect that spawns one.
- The result is the duplicate-writer outcome task-da89f620 demonstrates for the CLI: daemon pid 15 (container) and a second daemon (host) both serve one .moe/.
- docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:460 promises that host clients use the daemon.json the container writes. CLAUDE.md makes JetBrains the primary IDE, so it must not lag the daemon fix.

FIX DIRECTION
- Read the pidNamespace field task-da89f620 adds to daemon.json, in DaemonInfo (moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt:290) and parseDaemonInfo.
- Treat a record whose namespace differs from the plugin's own like isOtherSideOfWsl: skip the pid, and require the port plus the existing /health identity check (DaemonIdentityProbe). The plugin's own namespace is readlink of /proc/self/ns/pid on Linux. On another OS, or when the value cannot be read, any recorded value counts as different.
- Never delete a record, and never spawn, while that check answers for this project.
- offLoopbackBindRefusal (:957-975) and the other `isOtherSideOfWsl(...) || isProcessAlive(...)` sites (:317, :358, :386, :969) take the same rule.
- A record without the field keeps today's behavior.

PLACEMENT
- No open row holds MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt, MoeProjectService.kt or Models.kt (lanes.js -v at 12:10Z).
- dependsOn task-da89f620, which fixes the field's name and format.
- Run `./gradlew test` under the jetbrains-gradle lease (mem:gotcha-architect-cannot-take-gradle-lease).
definitionOfDone: MoeDaemonSupervisorTest (or MoeProjectForeignDaemonTest) covers a record from another pid namespace with a dead pid, an open port and /health naming this project. The test proves that isReachable is true and that neither the supervisor's start path nor MoeProjectService.connect() deletes daemon.json or spawns a daemon. The new cases fail on 2037e856.

A record without pidNamespace, or with the plugin's own namespace, keeps today's results: a dead pid is stale and gets deleted. The existing DaemonIdentity, foreign-daemon and supervisor tests pass unchanged.
`./gradlew test` in moe-jetbrains is green, with fresh results from a run under the jetbrains-gradle lease.

implementationPlan.description:
Model field and the supervisor rule. The edits are exact; an architect seat cannot dry-run Gradle (mem:gotcha-architect-cannot-take-gradle-lease).

(a) moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt, data class DaemonInfo (:290-297). Change the last parameter `val bindHost: String? = null` to `val bindHost: String? = null,` and append:
    // A Linux daemon records its pid namespace, `pid:[N]` (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts buildDaemonInfo, task-da89f620).
    val pidNamespace: String? = null
Gson leaves it null when the key is absent, so every positional DaemonInfo(...) in the tests still compiles.

(b) moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt.
1. Constructor: the last parameter `private val docSync: (File, Boolean) -> Unit = ::syncBundledDocs` gains a trailing comma, followed by:
    // This IDE's own pid namespace, injected by tests; null when it cannot be read (not Linux).
    private val ownPidNamespace: () -> String? = { readOwnPidNamespace() }
2. Companion object, beside isOtherSideOfWsl (:1025), add:
    // The daemon's pidNamespace format (packages/moe-daemon/src/server/probeHost.ts PID_NAMESPACE, task-da89f620).
    internal val PID_NAMESPACE = Regex("""^pid:\[[0-9]{1,20}\]$""")
    /** This process's pid namespace, readlink /proc/self/ns/pid on Linux; null when unreadable (not Linux) or malformed. Never throws. */
    internal fun readOwnPidNamespace(link: () -> String = { Files.readSymbolicLink(File("/proc/self/ns/pid").toPath()).toString() }): String? =
        try { link().takeIf { PID_NAMESPACE.matches(it) } } catch (_: Exception) { null }
3. Members beside isReachable (:948), add:
   - `fun isOtherPidNamespace(info: DaemonInfo): Boolean { val recorded = info.pidNamespace ?: return false; return PID_NAMESPACE.matches(recorded) && recorded != ownPidNamespace() }`
     KDoc: written in another pid namespace than this IDE's (a container, another WSL distro), so its pid names no process here. As for isOtherSideOfWsl, it is never probed or signalled and the port alone judges it. Only a well-formed pid:[N] counts (daemon.json is repository content). An absent or malformed value, or this IDE's own namespace, keeps the pid rules. With no readable own namespace, any recorded value differs.
   - `private fun pidUnjudgeable(info: DaemonInfo): Boolean = isOtherSideOfWsl(info.projectPath, isWindows()) || isOtherPidNamespace(info)`
4. Use it at every pid site:
   - :161 `if (isOtherSideOfWsl(info.projectPath, isWindows())) return false` becomes `if (pidUnjudgeable(info)) return false`. Never verify or replace such a daemon.
   - :317 in replacementMetadataCleared, `!isOtherSideOfWsl(info.projectPath, isWindows())` becomes `!pidUnjudgeable(info)`.
   - :949 in isReachable, `(isOtherSideOfWsl(info.projectPath, isWindows()) || isProcessAlive(info.pid))` becomes `(pidUnjudgeable(info) || isProcessAlive(info.pid))`.
   - :969 in offLoopbackBindRefusal, `isOtherSideOfWsl(info.projectPath, isWindows())` becomes `pidUnjudgeable(info)`. Its KDoc names a record from another pid namespace beside the WSL one.
5. stopDaemonForRestart (:349): right after the WSL refusal block and before `if (windowsRestart())`, add
    if (info != null && isOtherPidNamespace(info)) {
        return "Restart Daemon did not stop pid ${info.pid}, which .moe/daemon.json records in another pid namespace (for example a container): " +
            "this IDE can neither see nor signal that process. Stop that daemon where it runs (for example with docker stop), " +
            "then use Restart Daemon."
    }
   Today LEGACY destroys whatever host process holds that pid number. That is an unrelated process.
6. stopWindowsRestart (:386) is reached only after that early return, so it needs no change.
7. MoeProjectService.kt needs no edit: connect() (:177, :206) and connectWithRetry decide through isReachable.

Error handling: readOwnPidNamespace catches every exception. isOtherPidNamespace does a regex match and a string compare and never throws with the default provider. The existing try/catch wrappers around isReachable and offLoopbackBindRefusal stay.

- Add six tests beside the other-side ones (:281-325, :369-386, :412-438), mirroring them:
  - PN1 `PN1 isOtherPidNamespace counts only a well-formed namespace that is not this IDE's`:
    - With supervisor(root), "pid:[1]" is true.
    - null, "pid:[7]", "pid:[x]", "pid:[1", "net:[1]", " pid:[1]" and "pid:[" + "1".repeat(21) + "]" are false.
    - MoeDaemonSupervisor(root.canonicalPath, "Test", ownPidNamespace = { null }) makes "pid:[7]" true.
    - MoeDaemonSupervisor.readOwnPidNamespace { "pid:[7]" } is "pid:[7]". It is null for { "garbage" } and for { throw java.nio.file.NoSuchFileException("/proc/self/ns/pid") }.
  - PN2 `PN2 isReachable uses only the port for a record from another pid namespace`: mirror 'isReachable uses only the port for other-side pids'.
    - local = DaemonInfo(9876, 42, "now", root.canonicalPath, pidNamespace = "pid:[7]"), and namespaced = local.copy(pid = 43, pidNamespace = "pid:[1]").
    - For alive and open in {false, true}: isReachable(local) == alive && open, and isReachable(namespaced) == open.
    - The probed pids are exactly [42].
  - PN3 `PN3 ensureDaemonRunning leaves an open daemon from another pid namespace alone and replaces a closed one`: mirror 'leaves an open other-side daemon of this project alone' with DaemonInfo(9876, 42, "now", root.canonicalPath, pidNamespace = "pid:[1]").
    - Open: no start, bytes equal, no pid probed.
    - Closed: one start and the file deleted.
    - Call killSpawnedDaemon() as BH3 does.
  - PN4 `PN4 restart refuses metadata from another pid namespace without touching any process under either profile`: mirror 'restart refuses other-side metadata' with the same proxy handle and loops.
    - The exact refusal is "Restart Daemon did not stop pid 42, which .moe/daemon.json records in another pid namespace (for example a container): this IDE can neither see nor signal that process. Stop that daemon where it runs (for example with docker stop), then use Restart Daemon."
    - No probe, lookup or destroy happens.
    - Under LEGACY and !windows, the same record with pidNamespace "pid:[7]" returns null after exactly one probe, one lookup and one destroy (today).
  - PN5 `PN5 a record from another pid namespace bound off loopback never has its pid probed`: mirror BH3 with root.canonicalPath, bindHost = "::1" and pidNamespace = "pid:[1]", with probes answering alive.
    - Open: kept, no start.
    - Closed: replaced.
    - The probed list is always empty.
  - PN6 `PN6 a record without pidNamespace, malformed, or with this IDE's own keeps the pid rules`: for ns in listOf(null, "pid:[7]", "pid:[x]"), with a dead pid 42 and an open port:
    - isReachable is false.
    - ensureDaemonRunning() is true, with one start and the file deleted.
    - 42 was probed.
    - Call killSpawnedDaemon().

moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeProjectForeignDaemonTest.kt: two tests using the fixture's writeDaemonJson, healthReply, health, injectSupervisor and field helpers.
  - PN7 `PN7 connect keeps a reachable daemon json from another pid namespace and connects as today`:
    - f.healthReply(200, f.health(f.basePath)), then write f.writeDaemonJson("S1").copy(pidNamespace = "pid:[1]") as Gson JSON and keep its text.
    - Inject MoeDaemonSupervisor(f.basePath, "Test", portProbe = { _, _ -> true }, processAliveProbe = { probed += it; false }, processStarter = { error("must not spawn") }, ownPidNamespace = { "pid:[7]" }).

    - Set windowsRestartInFlight to true, exactly as BH5 does, so connect()'s own branch decides.
    - After connect(): daemon.json is gone, probed is empty, and f.service.field("reconnectFuture") is not null.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: The JetBrains plugin treats a .moe/daemon.json whose pidNamespace (pid:[N], written by the daemon since task-da89f620) differs from the IDE's own as it treats a record from the other side of the WSL boundary. It never probes or signals that pid, and the port alone decides reachability. An open port means the daemon is live: the start path neither replaces nor spawns, connect() keeps daemon.json and connects through the existing /health identity check, and Restart Daemon refuses with a message naming the other pid namespace. A closed port means the record is stale and is deleted and replaced, as today, so the IDE recovers once a container is gone. Records without the field, malformed ones and ones naming the IDE's own namespace keep today's pid rules.
invariants: No code path probes (isProcessAlive) or signals (processLookup/destroy) the pid of a record from another pid namespace.
isOtherSideOfWsl semantics and the existing other-side tests are unchanged.
Only pidNamespace values matching ^pid:\[[0-9]{1,20}\]$ count; null, malformed values and the IDE's own namespace keep the pid rules.
MoeProjectService.kt is unchanged; it decides through isReachable.
compatibility: DaemonInfo gains a trailing optional pidNamespace: String? = null, so every positional and named construction compiles, and Gson leaves it null for older daemon.json files.
No wire, settings or UI-contract change apart from the new Restart Daemon refusal text.

The JetBrains plugin treats a .moe/daemon.json whose pidNamespace (pid:[N], written since task-da89f620) differs from the IDE's own like a record from the other side of the WSL boundary. It never probes or signals that pid, and the port alone decides reachability.
